ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r1.claim: The Adam narrative is retold to alert his descendants to Satan’s snares and to add knowledge after the command to seek increase in knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r1.anchor: فكان في ذلك مزيد علم له عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r2.claim: The covenant given to Adam means a bequest or admonition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r3.claim: The omitted complement after before most likely means the people warned in the Qur’an, who broke God’s covenant and abandoned faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r3.anchor: تقديره من قبل هؤلاء الذين صرف لهم من الوعيد في القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r4.claim: Hasan understands before to mean before the Messenger and the Qur’an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: من قبل الرسول والقرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r5.speaker: قول آخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r5.claim: Another interpretation dates the event to before Adam ate from the tree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r5.anchor: وقيل: من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r6.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r6.claim: Al-Tabari reads Adam’s precedent as an example of how the Meccan unbelievers reject signs, disobey messengers, and follow Satan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r6.anchor: قال الطبري: المعنى أن يعرض يا محمد هؤلاء الكفرة عن آياتي ويخالفوا رسلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects making Adam a model for deniers because Adam sinned through interpretation; he instead allows an independent story or a warning parallel to Muhammad’s instruction not to hasten the Qur’an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف وذلك أن كون آدم مثالا للكفار الجاحدين بالله ليس بشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God warned Adam before humanity existed, and his failure to heed the threat establishes a pattern later followed by his descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r8.anchor: لقد أمرنا أباهم آدم ووصيناه أن لا يقرب الشجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r9.claim: The apparent meaning of Adam’s forgetting is that he left the command to guard against the tree and eat its fruit; al-Zamakhshari also allows literal forgetfulness from weak resolve, while Ibn Atiyya excludes absent-mindedness because it would not merit punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن النسيان هنا الترك إن ترك ما وصي به من الاحتراس عن الشجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r10.speaker: اليماني والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r10.claim: They read the verb in a passive form, meaning Satan caused Adam to forget; resolve means firm determination and persistence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p388/r10.anchor: وقرأ اليماني والأعمش فنسي بضم النون وتشديد السين أي نساه الشيطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that Adam lacked firm resolve to persist in abstaining from the tree; finding resolve can mean knowing it or being granted it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي على ترك الأكل وأن يتصلب في ذلك تصلبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r2.speaker: قول آخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r2.claim: Other explanations say Adam lacked resolve to sin, preserved the command, showed patience against eating, or lacked resolve in careful reasoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p389/r2.anchor: وقيل: حفظا لما أمر به. وقيل: صبرا عن أكل الشجرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r1.claim: ʿAhd means imposing a responsibility on someone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r2.claim: Adam’s haste illustrates the danger just raised for the Prophet; Moses’ haste also had bad results, so gradual preaching protects the community’s training from gaps Satan or Sāmirī could exploit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r2.anchor: it was this hastiness that made Adam (sws) commit a mistake

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r3.claim: Min qabl refers to the earlier Adam-and-Satan episode; past family history can guide present and future generations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r3.anchor: the past episode of Adam (sws) and Satan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r4.claim: Adam’s forgetting was a transient lapse under impatience; emotions are natural but must be bounded by patience and resolve, since unrestrained haste endangers people and society.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r4.anchor: all emotions are part of human nature

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r5.claim: The Qur’an describes human beings as hasty by nature, citing 21:37 and 17:11; haste benefits them only when controlled by patience and resolve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p75/r5.anchor: Haste is an emotion among others and it is found in human nature

ELMALILI:20:105-115/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r5.claim: He says God had made a covenant with Adam, who forgot it, and that Adam lacked resolve.
ELMALILI:20:105-115/r5.anchor: Fi’l-hakīka bundan evvel Âdem’e ahid verdik de unuttu ve Biz onda bir azim bulmadık

SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r1.speaker: اليماني
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r1.claim: Al-Yamani reads فنُسِّي with a doubled sīn and damma on the nūn, meaning Satan made Adam forget.
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r1.anchor: وقرأ اليماني " فنسي " بضم النون وتشديد السين بمعنى: نساه الشيطان.

SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r2.claim: وجد may mean knew and take two objects, supplied here as له and عزما.
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r2.anchor: فتتعدى لاثنين، وهما " له عزما " ، وأن تكون بمعنى الإصابة

SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r3.claim: Alternatively, وجد means encountered and takes only عزما as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r3.anchor: وأن تكون بمعنى الإصابة فتتعدى لواحد، وهو " عزما ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r4.claim: له can attach to وجد, or be an omitted circumstantial phrase describing عزما, originally its adjective but moved ahead.
SAMIN-DURR:20:115/r4.anchor: و " له " متعلق بالوجدان، أو بمحذوف على أنه حال من " عزما " إذ هو في الأصل

ASAD-NOTES:20:115/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:115/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:115/r1.claim: Adam forgot God's command and lacked firmness of purpose.
ASAD-NOTES:20:115/r1.anchor: but he forgot it, and We found no firmness of purpose in him

ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.claim: The commandment, more precisely a warning, is stated in 20:117.
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r1.anchor: The relevant divine commandment - or, rather, warning - is spelled out in verse 117.

ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r2.claim: The passage connects to 20:99, which introduces earlier stories, and uses Adam to illustrate a recurring human neglect of spiritual truths.
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r2.anchor: The present passage connects with the statement in verse 99

ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r3.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r3.claim: Razi reads the story as showing that neglect of spiritual truths recurs throughout human history, with Adam symbolizing humanity as elsewhere in the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:20:115#n102/r3.anchor: negligence of spiritual truths is one of the recurrent characteristics of the human race (Razi)

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r5.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads فنسي ولم without fatḥa on yāʾ; the author refers to his earlier discussion of pausal-style yāʾ-sukūn in an accusative position.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الأعمش: "فنسي ولم9"، ولا ينصب الياء.

NASHR:v1p419/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419/r1.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v1p419/r1.claim: Because no precedent was known for Ibn Dhakwān in أأعجمي and أأن كان, Makkī permits only separation between the two hamzas and analogizes his method to Hishām, following the transmitter paired with him.
NASHR:v1p419/r1.anchor: لكن ابن ذكوان لم نجد له أصلا يقاس عليه، فيجب أن يحمل أمره

NASHR:v1p419/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p419/r2.claim: The author found an explicit report that al-Hāshimī links the plural mīm before hamzat al-qaṭʿ, from al-Shahrazūrī and Ibn Khayrūn; this confirms his conclusion.
NASHR:v1p419/r2.anchor: ثم رأيت النص على الهاشمي المذكور لأبي الكرم الشهرزوري وأبي منصور بن خيرون بصلة ميم الجمع للهاشمي عند همزة القطع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says Adam forgot in the sense that he abandoned his Lord’s command.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ فنسي ﴾ قال ترك أمر ربه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r1.claim: After praising the Qur’an and urging care in receiving it, obeying its commands, and avoiding forgetfulness, the passage gives Adam’s lapse as an example.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r1.anchor: كأنه لما مدح سبحانه القرإن وحرض على استعمال التؤدة والرفق في اخذه وعهد على العزيمة بامره وترك النسيان فيه ضرب حديث إدم مثلا للنسيان وترك العزيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees an added warning to the Prophet against haste and lack of care, lest he fall into an error like Adam’s, linking this passage to the prohibition on haste.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r2.anchor: وذكر ابن عطية أن في ذلك مزيد تحذير للنبي ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) عن العجلة وعدم التؤدة لئلا يقع فيما لا ينبغي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects the story to the prior account of repeated warnings: the opponents ignored them and forgot, as their father Adam ignored and forgot his charge, showing disobedience as an ingrained pattern; al-Ṭabarī is also reported to say similarly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : هو عطف على ( صرفنا ) عطف القصة على القصة والتخالف فيه انشاء وخبرية لا يضر مع أن المقصود بالعطف جواب القسم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r4.claim: The repeated warning was meant to make people wary or remind them, but they disregarded and forgot it just as Adam forgot his charge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r4.anchor: وحاصل المعنى عليه صرفنا الوعيد وكررناه لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا لكنهم لم يلتفتوا لذلك ونسوه كما لم يلتفت أبوهم إلى الوعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that this reading diminishes Adam by making his story an example for deniers of God’s signs, since Adam acted on an interpretation; al-Ālūsī says the reading is sound and should stand.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r5.anchor: وتعقبه ابن عطية بأنه ضعيف لما فيه من الغضاضة من مقام آدم عليه السلام حيث جعلت قصته مثلا للجاحدين لآيات الله تعالى وهو عليه السلام إنما وقع منه ما وقع بتأويل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r6.claim: Abū Muslim links the story instead to ‘Thus We relate to you some accounts of what has preceded’; al-Ālūsī considers this reading weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : أنه عطف على قوله تعالى ( كذلك نقص عليك من انباء ما قد سبق ) وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers two other possibilities: connect the verse to ‘do not hasten,’ or treat it as a new, unrelated beginning; al-Ālūsī dismisses the latter as narrow-minded.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r7.anchor: واستظهر ابن عطية فيه أحد امرين التعلق بلا تعجل وكونه ابتداء كلام لا تعلق له بما قبله وهذا الأخير وإن قدمه في كلامه ناشئ من ضيق العطن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r8.claim: Here عهد means a charge or command: the king charged, enjoined, or instructed someone when he ordered and advised them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r8.anchor: والعهد الوصية يقال عهد اليه الملك ووغر اليه وعزم عليه وتقدم اليه إذا أمره ووصاه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r9.claim: The object of the charge is omitted but supplied by what follows; the lām answers an omitted oath: ‘By God, We charged him.’
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r9.anchor: والمعهود محذوف يدل عليه ما بعده واللام واقعة في جواب قسم محذوف أي واقسم بالله لقد أمرناه ووصيناه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r10.claim: ‘Before’ may mean before the present time, before the present opponents existed, before the Qur’an was revealed, or before Adam ate from the tree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r10.anchor: من قبل ( أي من قبل هذا الزمان وقيل : أي من قبل وجود هؤلاء المخالفين وعن الحسن أي من قبل إنزال القرآن وقيل : أي من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r11.claim: The apparent reading is that Adam forgot the charge by failing to attend to or preserve it; the reproach concerns his neglect of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r11.anchor: فنسى ( العهد ولم يهتم به ولم يشتغل بحفظه حتى غفل عنه والعتاب جاء من ترك الأهتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan take ‘forgot’ figuratively as abandoning the instruction to guard against the tree and refrain from its fruit.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والحسن أن المراد فترك ما وصى به من الأحتراس عن الشجرة وأكل ثمرتها فالنسيان مجاز عن ترك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r13.claim: The following فاء may show ordinary sequence, or be explanatory: he neglected the command and so forgot; the object of ‘forgot’ is omitted and supplied from context.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r13.anchor: والفاء للتعقيب وهو عرفي وقيل : فصيحة أي لم يهتم به فنسى والمفعول محذوف وهو ما أشرنا اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r14.claim: Other proposed omitted objects are the warning that eating would expel Adam from the garden, God’s statement that Satan was an enemy to him and his wife, or the proof that the prohibition addressed the species rather than an individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : المنسى الوعيد بخروج الجنة إن أكل وقيل قوله تعالى : ( إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك ) وقيل : الأستدلال على أن النهى عن الجنس دون الشخص

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r1.speaker: اليماني والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r1.claim: Al-Yamānī and al-Aʿmash read فنسى with a doubled, passive sīn: Satan caused Adam to forget.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ اليماني والأعمش ( فنسى ) بضم النون متشديد السين أي نساه الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r2.claim: ʿAzm means a firm decision, settled resolve, or steadiness in matters; the explanation fits both readings of ‘forgot.’
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r2.anchor: تصميم رأى وثبات قدم في الأمور وهذا جار على القولين في النسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda explain that Adam lacked the patience to refrain from eating from the tree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r3.anchor: وروى جماعة عن ابن عباس وقتادة أن المعنى لم تجد له صبرا عن أكل الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say Adam had no resolve to commit sin: he erred without intending it, fitting a literal sense of forgetfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r4.anchor: وعن ابن زيد وجماعة أن المعنى لم نجد له عزما على الذنب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس؛ عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells ʿUmar that ʿAlī did not intend to distress the Prophet by seeking Abū Jahl’s daughter while married to Fāṭima; like Adam, he lacked resolve to offend, since involuntary thoughts cannot be prevented and he would repent when corrected.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r5.anchor: وجاء عن ابن عباس ما يقتضيه فقد أخرج الزبير بن بكار في الموفقيات عنه قال قال لى عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه إن صاحبكم هذا يعني علي ابن أبي طالب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the interpretation as lack of intent is not immediate in the wording, fits the context poorly, and makes the clause repeat the preceding statement that Adam forgot.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r6.anchor: لكن لايخفى عليك أن هذا التفسير غير متبادر ولاكثير المناسبة للمقام وحاصل لم نجد الخ عليه أنه نسى فيتكرر مع ماقبله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r7.claim: If نجد means knowledge, عزما is its object and له is advanced; if it means finding in the sense opposite to nonexistence, له is attached to it, fronted from the object, or is a circumstantial phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p269#3/r7.anchor: ثم أن ( لم نجد ) أن كان من الوجود العلمى فله عز ما مفعولا مقدم الثاني على الأول لكونه ظرفا وإن كان من الوجود المقابل للعدم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.claim: God commanded and revealed to Adam not to eat from the tree, before the people who broke their covenant and abandoned faith, mentioned at 20:113.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.anchor: أمرناه وأوحينا إليه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة من قبل هؤلاء الذين نقضوا عهدك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.claim: Adam left the command; the comparison is that those people broke their covenant just as Adam had forgotten his.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.anchor: فترك الأمر، والمعنى أنهم نقضوا العهد، فإن آدم أيضا عهدنا إليه فنسي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that Adam lacked patience to refrain from what had been forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن لم نجد له صبرا عما نهي عنه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.speaker: عطية العوفي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī explains the phrase as lack of retention of what Adam had been commanded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.anchor: وقال عطية العوفي: حفظا لما أمر به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says Adam lacked firm resolve when he obeyed his envious enemy Iblīs, who had refused to prostrate to him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: رأيا معزوما حيث أطاع عدوه إبليس الذي حسده وأبى أن يسجد له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r9.claim: In Arabic, resolve is the settling of the self upon an action.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r9.anchor: و"العزم" في اللغة: هو توطين النفس على الفعل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r10.claim: Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī says Adam’s forbearance would outweigh that of all his descendants combined.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو أمامة الباهلي: لو وزن حلم آدم بحلم جميع ولده لرجح حلمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r11.claim: In answer to whether Adam forgot God’s command, the author says he may have forgotten it and still been accountable, since forgetfulness had not then been lifted from people; it was lifted from this community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r11.anchor: قيل: يجوز أن يكون نسي أمره، ولم يكن النسيان في ذلك الوقت مرفوعا عن الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r12.claim: Another view is that Adam forgot God’s punishment and thought the prohibition was only for commendation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p297#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: نسي عقوبة الله وظن أنه نهي تنزيها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r7.claim: God's covenant to Adam was a command; عهد إليه is used for commanding and enjoining.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r7.anchor: ولقد أمرناه يقال تقدم الملك إليه وأوعز إليه وعزم عليه وعهد إليه إذا أمره

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r8.claim: The emphatic lām answers an unexpressed oath.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r8.anchor: واللام جواب قسم محذوف وإنما عطف قصة آدم على قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r9.claim: Adam's story is linked to 46:27 to show that human nature is deeply rooted in disobedience and forgetfulness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r9.anchor: للدلالة على أن أساس بني آدم على العصيان وعرقهم راسخ في النسيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r10.claim: Min qabl means before this time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r10.anchor: من قبل هذا الزمان. { فنسى } العهد ولم يعن به

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r11.claim: Adam either forgot and neglected the covenant or abandoned the instruction to keep away from the tree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r11.anchor: العهد ولم يعن به حتى غفل عنه، أو ترك ما وصي به من الاحتراز عن الشجرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r12.claim: ʿAzm is firmness of judgment; with such resolve, Satan could not have misled Adam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r12.anchor: تصميم رأي وثباتا على الأمر إذ لو كان ذا عزيمة وتصلب لم يزله الشيطان

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r13.claim: Bayḍāwī suggests this may have been at the beginning of Adam's life, before experience taught him hardship and ease.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r13.anchor: ولعل ذلك كان في بدء أمره قبل أن يجرب الأمور ويذوق شريها وأريها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r14.claim: The Prophet reportedly said Adam's intellect would outweigh that of his descendants if they were weighed, despite this verse's statement about his resolve.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r14.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r15.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r15.claim: Another view understands ʿazm as intention to sin, since Adam erred without deliberate intent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r15.anchor: وقيل عزما على الذنب لأنه أخطأ ولم يتعمده

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r16.claim: If najid means know, lahu and ʿazman are its two objects; if it means find, lahu is circumstantial or governed by the verb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:114-115/r16.anchor: ونجد إن كان من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم فله عزما مفعولاه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.claim: The Moses story displays God's patience with servants who forget covenants; after praising the Reminder, condemning those who turn away, and instructing the Prophet about it, the sūra turns to Adam to warn against forgetfulness and urge repentance, showing God's ancient practice of forbearance toward inherently deficient people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p48/r15.anchor: أتبع ذلك سبحانه قصة آدم عليه السلام تحذيرا من الركون إلى ما يسبب النسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r1.claim: Biqai connects the verse either with the earlier statement that God sent down an Arabic judgment (13:37) or with the promise to recount past histories, reaffirming the Qur'anic instruction and fulfilling that promise.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r2.claim: God's earlier covenant with Adam, the father of humanity, prohibited eating from the tree; Adam forgot it and ate despite knowing God's majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r2.anchor: أبي البشر الذي أطلعناه على كثير منها في النهي عن الأكل من الشجرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r3.claim: Because Adam held an exalted rank, his lapse was counted as a sin, following the maxim that the good deeds of the righteous are the faults of those brought near.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r3.anchor: فعددنا عليه وقوعه في ذلك المنهي ناسيا ذنبا لعلو رتبته عندنا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r4.claim: Adam lacked a firm, decisive purpose and unwavering will of the sort attributed to angels; God did not know such resolve to be present in him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r4.anchor: أي قصدا صلبا ماضيا وإرادة نافذة لا تردد فيها كإرادات الملائكة عليهم السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r5.claim: Despite the lapse, God forgave Adam and did not remove him from the rank of the chosen.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p50/r5.anchor: ومع ذلك عفونا عنه ولم نزحوحه عن رتبة الاصطفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.claim: The sūra's purpose is to show God's forbearance toward those who stray and His power over rejecters; Adam's failure is first summarized and then detailed, naming it disobedience to warn against forbidden acts and direct the deficient toward prompt repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p51/r1.anchor: ذكر فعله آدم عليه السلام هذه في هذه السورة بلفظ المعصية مع التصريح بأنها وجه النسيان , وذكر ذلك أولا مجملا ثم أتبعه تفصيله

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the word insan as derived from the fact that Adam was charged with a covenant and then forgot.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: إنما سمي الإنسان: لأنه عهد إليه فنسي

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r5.claim: Abu Umama says Adam's forbearance outweighed that of all humanity combined; he glosses the verse's lack of resolve as deficient retention.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي قال: لو أن أحلام بني آدم جمعت منذ يوم خلق آدم إلى أن تقوم الساعة فوضعت في كفة وحلم آدم في كفة لرجح حلمه بأحلامهم ثم قال الله: {ولم نجد له عزما} قال: حفظا

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says Adam's intelligence equaled that of all his descendants, so the verse's mention of forgetting does not imply lack of intelligence.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r6.anchor: عن الحسن قال: كان عقل آدم مثل عقل جميع ولده قال الله: {فنسي ولم نجد له عزما}

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the covenant instructed Adam not to approach the tree.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم} قال: أن لا يقرب الشجرة

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses resolve as retention or memory.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} قال: حفظا

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets forgetting as abandoning the command and says God had not endowed Adam with resolve.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {فنسي} قال: فترك {ولم نجد له عزما} يقول: لم نجعل له عزما

DURR-FULL:v5p602/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that migrants with uncertain lineage wished for revelation about their ancestry, prompting the verse forbidding questions whose answers would distress them; the account continues in the next segment.
DURR-FULL:v5p602/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: سألت عمر بن الخطاب

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report to Umar, Umar worries that Ali's asceticism could be undone by self-admiration; discussing Ali's wish to marry Abu Jahl's daughter while married to Fatima, Ibn Abbas says Ali had not resolved to anger the Prophet and would repent when alerted, comparing fleeting thoughts with Adam's lack of resolve.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r1.anchor: ثم قال لي: إن صاحبكم هذا - يعني علي بن أبي طالب - أن ولي زهد ولكني أخشى عجب نفسه

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r2.claim: Umar explains forgetting as occurring when a cloud-like darkness covers the heart; when it clears, a person remembers what he had forgotten.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال لعمر بن الخطاب: يا أمير المؤمنين لم يذكر الرجل ولم ينس فقال: إن على القلب طخاة كطخاة القمر فإذا تغشت القلب نسي ابن آدم

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas forbids eating or drinking with the left hand, saying Adam ate with it, forgot, and passed that forgetfulness down.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه قال: لا تأكلوا بشمائلكم ولا تشربوا بشمائلكم فإن آدم أكل بشماله فنسي

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r4.speaker: عطية
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r4.claim: Atiyya glosses resolve as retaining what Adam had been commanded.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r4.anchor: عن عطية {ولم نجد له عزما} قال: حفظا لما أمر به

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} قال: صبرا

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says Adam's forbearance would equal the forbearance of all scholars if weighed against it.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: لو وزن حلم آدم بحلم العالمين لوزنه

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says Adam was not one of the messengers designated as firmly resolute.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r7.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير قال: لم يكن آدم من أولي العزم

DURR-FULL:v5p603/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says Adam abandoned the warning; if this had been mere forgetfulness, he would not be liable, since God has lifted forgetfulness and error from believers.
DURR-FULL:v5p603/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فنسي} قال: ترك ما قدم إليه ولو كان منه نسيان ما كان عليه شيء لأن الله قد وضع عن المؤمنين النسيان والخطأ ولكن آدم ترك ما قدم إليه من أكل الشجرة

BURSEVI:v5p333/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r1.claim: To covenant with someone is to entrust and charge them to preserve something; a covenant is its continual guarding and care, and can be binding by law or by a promise such as a vow.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r1.anchor: يقال : عهد فلان إلى فلان بعهد أي : ألقى العهد إليه وأوصاه بحفظه والعهد حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا بعد حال

BURSEVI:v5p333/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r2.claim: God’s covenant may be planted in reason, delivered through scripture and prophets, or voluntarily undertaken without being originally binding in religious law.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r2.anchor: وعهد الله تارة يكون بما ركزه في عقولنا وتارة يكون بما أمرنا به بكتابه وبألسنة رسله وتارة بما نلتزمه وليس بلازم في أصل الشرع

BURSEVI:v5p333/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r3.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p333/r3.claim: One proposed etymology derives Adam’s name from the surface of the earth from which his body was made.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r3.anchor: قيل سمي بذلك لكون جسده من أديم الأرض

BURSEVI:v5p333/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r4.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p333/r4.claim: Another proposal derives the name from the brownness of his complexion, as ādam can mean brown.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r4.anchor: وقيل لسمرة في لونه يقال رجل آدم نحو أسمر

BURSEVI:v5p333/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r5.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p333/r5.claim: Another proposal connects Adam with the mixture of different elements and powers in him, using the expression for blending someone into a family.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r5.anchor: وقيل سمي بذلك لكونه من عناصر مختلفة وقوى مفترقة يقال جعلت فلانا أدمة أهلي أي : خلطته بهم

BURSEVI:v5p333/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r6.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p333/r6.claim: Another proposal connects the name with the spirit, intellect, understanding, and vision that made Adam superior to others, using the word for what seasons food.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r6.anchor: وقيل سمي بذلك لما طيب به من الروح المنفوخ فيه وجعل له من العقل والفهم والرؤية

BURSEVI:v5p333/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r7.claim: Bursevi says the likeliest view is that Adam is a foreign word.

BURSEVI:v5p333/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r8.claim: God commanded and advised Adam not to eat from the familiar, specified tree, which will be explained after this verse.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r8.anchor: والمعنى وبالله لقد أمرناه ووصيناه بأن لا يأكل من الشجرة وهي المعهودة ويأتي بيانه بعد هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v5p333/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r9.claim: Min qablu means before that time.

BURSEVI:v5p333/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r10.claim: Adam forgot the covenant and failed to attend to it until it slipped from mind; nisyān may mean not remembering or deliberately abandoning something as though forgotten.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r10.anchor: {فنسى} العهد ولم يهتم به حتى غفل عنه والنسيان بمعنى عدم الذكر أو تركه ترك المنسى عنه

BURSEVI:v5p333/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r11.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p333/r11.claim: Al-Raghib defines forgetfulness as losing what was entrusted through weak memory, heedlessness, or deliberate neglect; blameworthy forgetfulness begins in intent, while excused forgetfulness is unintentional.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r11.anchor: قال الراغب النسيان ترك الإنسان ضبط ما استودع إما لضعف قلبه وإما عن غفلة أو عن قصد

BURSEVI:v5p333/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r12.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p333/r12.claim: The author invokes the report that error and forgetfulness have been lifted from the Muslim community for the kind of lapse that was not caused by the person.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r12.anchor: وما عذر فيه نحو ما روى "رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان" فهو ما لم يكن

BURSEVI:v5p333/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r13.claim: If wajada means knowing, lahu and ʿazman are its two objects, with the adverbial object advanced; the alternative sense of finding is more fitting because the absence of resolve is the point.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r13.anchor: إن كان من الوجود العلمي فله وعزما مفعولاه وقدم الثاني على الأول لكونه ظرفا وإن كان من الوجود المقابل للعدم وهو الأنسب

BURSEVI:v5p333/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r14.claim: ʿAzm is settling the self on an action and the heart on carrying a matter through.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r14.anchor: والعزم في اللغة توطين النفس على الفعل وعقد القلب على إمضاء الأمر

BURSEVI:v5p333/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r15.claim: God did not find Adam firmly resolved, steadfast in affairs, careful to preserve the command, and determined to fulfill it; otherwise Satan could not have misled him.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r15.anchor: لم نعلم أو لم نصادف له تصميم رأى وثبات قدم في الأمور ومحافظة على ما أمر به وعزيمة على القيامة به إذ لو كان كذلك لما أزله الشيطان

BURSEVI:v5p333/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r16.claim: Adam’s lapse occurred at the beginning, before he had experienced life’s bitter and sweet turns, and did not stem from deficient intelligence.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r16.anchor: وقد كان ذلك منه عليه السلام في بدء أمره من قبل أن يجرب الأمور ويتولى حارها وقارها ويذوق شريها وأريها لا من نقصان عقله

BURSEVI:v5p333/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333/r17.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p333/r17.claim: A hadith says that if the intellects of Adam’s children were weighed against Adam’s, Adam’s would outweigh theirs; the point is that even he was affected by Satan’s whispering.
BURSEVI:v5p333/r17.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "لو وزنت أحلام بني آدم بحلم آدم لرجح حلمه" وقد قال الله تعالى : {ولم نجد له عزما}

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r1.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r1.claim: Hafez’s couplet says Satan’s snare is strong without God’s grace, and Adam could not otherwise gain advantage over Satan.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r1.anchor: دام سختست مكر لطف خدا يا رشود ورنه آدم نبرد صرفه ز شيطان رجيم

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r2.claim: One view says forgetfulness was not yet lifted from human beings in Adam’s time, so he was accountable for it, whereas it was lifted for later people.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r2.anchor: قيل : لم يكن النسيان في ذلك الوقت مرفوعا عن الإنسان فكان مؤاخذا به وإنما رفع عنا

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r3.claim: The inward reading takes the first covenant as exclusive devotion to God, not attaching oneself to or obeying anything besides Him.

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r4.claim: When Adam entered the garden and saw its delights, he forgot the covenant, attached himself to the tree, and followed Satan.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r4.anchor: فلما دخل الجنة ونظر إلى نعيمها {فنسى} عهدنا وتعلق بالشجرة وانقاد للشيطان

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r5.claim: The inward reading says the divine manifestation of all God’s attributes overwhelmed and veiled Adam’s created qualities, leaving no resolve to attach himself to anything else.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r5.anchor: يشير إلى أن الله تعالى لما خلق آدم وتجلى فيه بجميع صفاته صارت ظلمات صفات خليقته مغلوبة مستورة بسطوات تجلى أنوار صفات الربوبية

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r6.claim: When animal and human desires stirred and Adam occupied himself with satisfying appetites, he forgot to discharge his duties; deeds layered darkness over the lights of knowledge and gnosis.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r6.anchor: فلما تحركت فيه دواعي البشرية الحيوانية وتداعت الشهوات النفسانية الإنسانية واشتغل باستيفاء الحظوظ نسي أداء الحقوق

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r7.claim: The inward commentary links nās, people, with nisyān, forgetfulness: people forgot God’s covenants and attached themselves to the forbidden tree.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r7.anchor: ولهذا سمي الناس ناسا لأنه ناس فنشأت له من تلك العاملات ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r8.speaker: العلامة
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r8.claim: An unnamed scholar’s verse reminds people that forgetfulness is habitual and exhorts them to remember and soften their hearts.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r8.anchor: قال العلامة : يا إنيسان عادتك النسيان أذكر الناس ناسس وأرق القلوب قاسس

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r9.speaker: أبو الفتح البستي
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Fath al-Busti’s apology to a leader says he forgot a promise, asks forgiveness, and notes that the first forgetful person was the first human.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو الفتح البستي في الاعتذار من النسيان إلى بعض الرؤساء : يا أكثر الناس إحسانا إلى الناس

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r10.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r10.claim: Ali is cited for ten causes of forgetfulness: excessive worry, cupping at the nape, stagnant-water urination, sour apples, coriander, mouse leftovers, reading grave tablets, seeing a crucified person, walking between tethered camels, and releasing a louse alive.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r10.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه : عشرة يورثن النيسان

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r11.speaker: قاضي خان
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r11.claim: Qadi Khan says there is no harm in releasing a louse alive, though proper manners are to kill it.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r11.anchor: لكن في قاضي خان لا بأس بطرح القملة حية والأدب أن يقتلها

BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r12.speaker: المقاصد الحسنة
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r12.claim: Al-Maqasid al-Hasana adds chewing gum as a cause of forgetfulness in men unless medically useful for bad breath; it is not disliked for a nonfasting woman, since it cleans teeth and firms gums like a siwak and her teeth are more delicate.
BURSEVI:v5p333#2/r12.anchor: وزاد في المقاصد الحسنة مضغ العلك أي : للرجال إذا لم يكن من علة كالبخر ولا يكره للمرأة إن لم تكن صائمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r1.claim: After the Moses story served as a warning to the Prophet’s deniers, the Adam story follows the request for increased knowledge to show another instructive account of Satan’s activity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r1.anchor: أعقبت تلك القصة بقصة آدم عليه السلام وما عرض له به الشيطان ، تحقيقا لفائدة قوله { وقل رب زدني علما }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r2.claim: The oath particle and emphatic lām foreground the parallel between Adam’s breach of covenant and Israel’s earlier breach of God’s covenant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r2.anchor: وافتتاح الجملة بحرف التحقيق ولام القسم لمجرد الاهتمام بالقصة تنبيها على قصد التنظير بين القصتين في التفريط في العهد ، لأن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r3.claim: Both stories feature Satan’s work: Israel’s account says the soul prompted the deed, while Adam’s says Satan whispered to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r3.anchor: وفي كون ذلك من عمل الشيطان كما قال في القصة الأولى { وكذلك سولت لي نفسي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r4.claim: The stories also parallel one another in forgetting what should have been guarded and remembered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r4.anchor: وفي أن في القصتين نسيانا لما يجب الحفاظ عليه وتذكره فقال في القصة الأولى { فنسي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r5.claim: من قبل omits its genitive complement, indicated by قبل being built on ḍamma; possible completions are before Moses was sent or before the previously mentioned events.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r5.anchor: فقوله { من قبل } حذف ما أضيف إليه ( قبل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r6.claim: If قبل means before what was mentioned, the covenant may be Moses’ commission and warning or the covenant with Israel recalled when Moses returned angry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p318/r6.anchor: والذي ذكر : إما عهد موسى الذي في قوله تعالى : { وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r1.claim: The covenant given to Adam was the warning in the garden, where he forgot it; its content is specified later in the passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r1.anchor: والمراد بالعهد إلى آدم : العهد إليه في الجنة التي أنسي فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r2.claim: Here forgetting means deliberately neglecting to act on the covenant, hence disobedience, as in the account of the Samaritan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r2.anchor: والنسيان : أطلق هنا على إهمال العمل بالعهد عمدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r3.claim: The account of Adam’s disobedience is supported by his exchange with Satan, who falsely swore he was a sincere adviser.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r3.anchor: وهو الذي يقتضيه قوله تعالى : { وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r4.claim: عزم is firm resolve to act without hesitation, overcoming an inclination to desist because the deed is difficult or another course is preferred.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r4.anchor: والعزم : الجزم بالفعل وعدم التردد فيه ، وهو مغالبة ما يدعو إليه الخاطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r5.claim: The author connects عزم to resolve in divorce, reliance after a decision, and the resolve of the steadfast messengers, whom he lists as Noah, Abraham, Ishmael, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r5.anchor: وهم نوح ، وإبراهيم ، وإسماعيل ، ويعقوب ، ويوسف ، وأيوب ، وموسى ، وداوود ، وعيسى عليهم السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r6.claim: Not finding resolve means Adam lacked the disposition to fulfill the command and override the impulse toward disobedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r6.anchor: والمراد هنا : العزم على امتثال الأمر وإلغاء ما يحسن إليه عدم الامتثال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r7.claim: The wording depicts a search for Adam’s resolve that fails to find it, representing the absence of resolve as though it were an object sought.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r7.anchor: واستعمل نفي وجدان العزم عند آدم في معنى عدم وجود العزم من صفته فيما عهد إليه تمثيلا لحال طلب حصوله عنده بحال الباحث على عزمه فلم يجده عنده بعد البحث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r9.claim: Alternatively, the covenant sentence may conclude the account of Aaron and the Samaritan: قبل means before Aaron, who lacked resolve to preserve Moses’ trust; the Adam story then begins separately.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p319/r9.anchor: وتكون جملة { ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل } تذييلا لقصة هارون مع السامري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari makes Adam a precedent for Muhammad's unbelieving opponents turning from revelation and following Satan; Ibn Atiyya rejects this because Adam sinned through interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.anchor: قال الطبري المعنى وإن يعرض يا محمد هؤلاء الكفرة عن آياتي ويخالفوا رسلي ويطيعوا إبليس فقدما فعل ذلك أبوهم آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.claim: The passage may begin a new story or connect to the command that Muhammad not rush the Qur'an: Adam's lapse then strengthens the warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.anchor: وإما أن يجعل تعلقه أنه لما عهد إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن لا يعجل بالقرآن مثل له بنبي قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.claim: Here عهد means a charge or testament.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.claim: Here نسي means “left aside,” not absent-mindedness, since the mentally forgetful are not liable to punishment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r5.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r5.claim: Al-A'mash reads the yāʾ with sukūn for ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «فنسي» بسكون الياء ووجهها طلب الخفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r6.claim: ʿAzm is persistence in conviction; Adam believed he should not eat from the tree but did not remain firm when Satan tempted him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r6.anchor: «العزم» المضي على المعتقد في أي شيء كان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r7.claim: Some explain ʿazm as patience, preservation, or other qualities; Ibn Atiyya says these exceed its precise sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r7.anchor: وعبر بعض المفسرين عن العزم هنا بالصبر وبالحفظ وبغير ذلك مما هو أعم من حقيقة العزم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r8.claim: Adam was charged not to approach the tree and told that Iblis was his enemy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r8.anchor: والشيء الذي عهد إلى آدم هو أن يقرب الشجرة وأعلم مع ذلك أن إبليس عدو له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r9.claim: Abu Umama says all human discernment from creation to the Resurrection would weigh less than Adam's discernment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p66#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة لو أن أحلام بني آدم وضعت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r1.claim: God had commanded and charged Adam not to eat from the tree; “before” contrasts him with those who later broke the covenant and abandoned faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r1.anchor: أي أمرناه وأوصيناه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say nasiya means that Adam abandoned what he had been commanded to do.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه الترك قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والمعنى ترك ما أمر به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi reports the alternative that Adam forgot in the ordinary sense, contrary to remembering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه من النسيان الذي يخالف الذكر حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r4.speaker: معاذ القارئ وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r4.claim: Muʿadh al-Qari, ʿAsim al-Jahdari, and Ibn al-Sumayfa read with ḍamma on nūn and a doubled sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ معاذ القارئ وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع فنسي برفع النون وتشديد السين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r5.claim: In Arabic, ʿazm is resolving inwardly to carry out an act.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r5.anchor: العزم في اللغة توطين النفس على الفعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r6.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that Adam lacked retention and did not keep in memory what he was ordered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r6.anchor: أحدها لم نجد له حفظا رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس والمعنى لم يحفظ ما أمر به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r7.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r7.claim: Qatada and Muqatil interpret Adam's lack of resolve as a failure to be patient and refrain from the forbidden act.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r7.anchor: والثاني صبرا قاله قتادة ومقاتل والمعنى لم يصبر عما نهي عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r8.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Saib says Adam lacked firmness; Ibn al-Anbari clarifies this concerns eating only and does not remove Adam from the class of resolute prophets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r8.anchor: والثالث حزما قاله ابن السائب قال ابن الأنباري وهذا لا يخرج آدم من أولي العزم وإنما لم يكن له عزم في الأكل فحسب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r9.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi gives the fourth view: Adam lacked resolve to return to the sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p327#2/r9.anchor: والرابع عزما في العود إلى الذنب ذكره الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the human being was named insan because he was charged with a covenant and then forgot it; Ibn Kathir notes another transmission from Ibn Abbas through Ali ibn Abi Talha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r1.anchor: قال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا أحمد بن سنان، حدثنا أسباط بن محمد، حدثنا الأعمش، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: إنما سمي الإنسان لأنه عهد إليه فنسي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r2.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan understand nasiya here to mean that Adam abandoned or neglected the command.

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r4.claim: Resolve is the heart’s commitment to do something; in the author’s view it belongs to the genus of will but is a prior willing that prepares the self for action.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r4.anchor: والعزم: عقد القلب على الشيء ليفعله، وهو العزيمة، وهو من جنس الإرادة عندنا إلا أنه إرادة متقدمة

JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.claim: A further connection warns the Prophet not to hasten or forget as Adam did; one need not marvel at forgetfulness, since Adam, his father, also forgot.
JISHUMI:v7p4748/r12.anchor: وقيل: لا تعجل ولا تنس هذا كما نسي آدم، فلا غرو إن نسيت فقد نسي آدم أبوك

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r1.claim: Adam may have forgotten because a long time passed; another explanation, which the author identifies as the sound view, says he took the prohibition to concern the individual tree rather than the whole class.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r1.anchor: وقيل: نسي لطول الزمان، وقيل: كان النهي عن الجنس، فنسي وظن أن النهي عن العين، وهو الوجه

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r2.speaker: قتادة، ومقاتل
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r2.claim: Qatada and Muqatil explain lack of resolve as lacking steadfast commitment or patience.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r2.anchor: عقدا ثابتا، وقيل: صبرا، عن قتادة، ومقاتل

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r3.speaker: عطية
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r3.claim: Atiyya explains it as failing to preserve what he had been commanded and entrusted with.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r3.anchor: وقيل: حفظا لما أمر به وجزاء، عن عطية

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd explains the phrase as not maintaining God’s command and holding fast to it.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r4.anchor: وقيل: محافظة على أمر الله وتمسكا به، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r5.claim: Other explanations are a firm intention and resolve to return to sin, or resolve to commit disobedience, though Adam acted forgetfully.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r5.anchor: وقيل: إصرارا وإضمارا عن العود إلى الذنب، وقيل: عزما على المعصية، وإنما فعله نسيانا

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r6.claim: If the alternative account is followed, Adam forgot the warning that eating would expel him from the Garden, the warning that Satan was his enemy, or the inference that the prohibition covered the whole class.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r6.anchor: قيل: نسي الوعيد، وأنه يخرج من الجنة إن أكل، وقيل: نسي قوله (إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك)

JISHUMI:v7p4751/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r14.claim: The account permits minor sins by prophets; nasiya here means leaving or neglecting, since actual forgetfulness cannot be subject to religious obligation.
JISHUMI:v7p4751/r14.anchor: على جواز الصغائر على الأنبياء، ومعنى (نسي) ترك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r1.claim: In royal commands and instructions, تقدم إلى, أوعز إلى, عزم على, and عهد إلى are expressions for issuing an order or charge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r1.anchor: يقال في أوامر الملوك ووصاياهم : تقدم الملك إلى فلان وأوعز إليه ، وعزم عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r2.claim: Adam's story follows the warning in 20:113: God had commanded him not to approach the tree and threatened him with the wrongdoers if he did, before the later people were warned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r2.anchor: عطف الله سبحانه قصة آدم على قوله : { وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r3.claim: نسي may mean forgetfulness, caused by failing to attend sincerely and secure the command in one's heart, or neglecting and abandoning the instruction to avoid the tree and its fruit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يراد النسيان الذي هو نقيض الذكر ، وأنه لم يعن بالوصية العناية الصادقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r4.claim: A reading vocalizes فَنُسِّي, making Satan the one who caused Adam to forget.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r5.claim: عزم is firm resolve and persistence in refraining from eating, strong enough to leave Satan no hope of tempting him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r5.anchor: العزم : التصميم والمضي على ترك الأكل ، وأن يتصلب في ذلك تصلبا يؤيس الشيطان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r6.claim: نجد may mean know, with له عزما as its two objects, or mean find as the opposite of lose, yielding the sense that Adam had no resolve.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p91/r6.anchor: والوجود : يجوز أن يكون بمعنى العلم ، ومفعولاه { له عزما } وأن يكون نقيض العدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r1.anchor: يعني فترك أمر ربه , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r2.claim: Alternatively, Adam forgot through ordinary forgetfulness or lapse; Ibn Abbas says humans are named from his forgetting after receiving the command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r2.anchor: أنه نسي من النسيان والسهو , قال ابن عباس : إنما أخذ الإنسان من أنه عهد إليه فنسي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r6.speaker: ابن أمامة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r6.claim: Ibn Umama says Adam's forbearance would outweigh that of humanity if their deeds were compared, despite the verse saying God found no resolve in him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r6.anchor: قال ابن أمامة : لو قرنت أعمال بني آدم بحلم آدم لرجح حلمه على حلمهم , وقد قال الله : { ولم نجد له عزما }

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r7.claim: A further sense is that Adam lacked resolve to return to the sin a second time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p429/r7.anchor: عزما في العودة إلى الذنب ثانيا

MUJAHID:v1p404/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p404/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
MUJAHID:v1p404/r1.claim: Abu Umama says Adam's forbearance would outweigh the combined intellects of all his descendants, in connection with God's saying that He found no resolve in Adam.
MUJAHID:v1p404/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي قال لو ان احلام بني آدم كلهم جمعت فجعلت في كفة وحلم آدم في كفة

MUQATIL:20:115-118/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r1.claim: Before Muhammad, God charged Adam not to eat from the tree.

MUQATIL:20:115-118/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r2.claim: Nasiya means Adam abandoned the charge, as do the same verb forms in 20:88, 32:14, and 5:14.

MUQATIL:20:115-118/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:115-118/r3.claim: Adam had no endurance to refrain from eating from the tree.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r1.claim: God’s covenant with Adam was a revelation and command not to eat from the tree.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r1.anchor: أي أوحينا اليه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r2.claim: In Arabic, a king’s order or counsel may be described as his advancing a command to someone or making a covenant with him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r2.anchor: يقال في أوامر الملوك ووصاياهم تقدم الملك إلى فلان وأوصى إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r3.claim: Adam’s story is joined to the preceding warnings; the oath stresses that God commanded their forefather not to approach the tree.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r3.anchor: فعطف قصة آدم على وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد والمعنى واقسم قسما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r4.claim: “Before” means before Adam’s descendants existed; Adam violated the prohibition just as they would, making this a rooted pattern in human conduct.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r4.anchor: من قبل وجودهم فخالف إلى ما نهى عنه كما أنهم يخالفون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r5.claim: He forgot the covenant, meaning the prohibition.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r6.claim: Prophets are accountable for forgetfulness they could have prevented by taking care to remember.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r6.anchor: والانبياء عليهم السلام يؤاخذون بالنسيان الذي لو تكلفوا لحفظوه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r7.claim: One explanation is that Adam did not deliberately intend to defy God’s command.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r8.claim: An alternative takes the phrase to mean that Adam was not among the people of firm resolve.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r8.anchor: أو لم يكن آدم من أولي العزم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r9.claim: “We found” may mean “we knew,” with “for him” and “resolve” as its two objects; or it may mean “exist,” with “for him” attached to the verb.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p69#4/r9.anchor: والوجود بمعنى العلم ومفعولاه له عزما أو بمعنى نقيض العدم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r1.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash has a variant reading of فنسي with the yāʾ quiescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r1.anchor: قرأ الأعمش باختلاف عنه «فنسي» بإسكان الياء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r2.claim: Mujāhid and most commentators take نسي to mean Adam left or neglected the command, as in 9:67.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r2.anchor: أحدهما: ترك أي ترك الأمر والعهد وهذا قول مجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes نسي as genuine forgetfulness: a human was made from a covenant he then forgot.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r3.anchor: وثانيهما قال ابن عباس: «نسي» هنا من السهو والنسيان، وإنما أخذ الإنسان من أنه عهد إليه فنسي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Adam forgot God's charge; had he been firm, he would not have obeyed Iblīs.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: نسي ما عهد الله إليه في ذلك، ولو كان له عزم ما أطاع عدوه إبليس.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r5.claim: On this view, Adam could have been subject to forgetfulness then, though forgetfulness is lifted from people today.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا القول يحتمل أن يكون آدم عليه السلام في ذلك الوقت مأخوذا بالنسيان

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r6.claim: من قبل means before Adam ate from the forbidden tree.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r6.anchor: ومعنى «من قبل» أي من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة لأنه نهي عنها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r7.speaker: القشيري والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī and al-Ṭabarī present the passage as consolation for the Prophet: human obedience to Satan is ancient, and Adam too broke a charge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r7.anchor: أي إن نقض هؤلاء العهد فإن آدم أيضا عهدنا إليه فنسي حكاه القشيري وكذلك الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects making Adam a model for unbelievers who knowingly deny God: Adam sinned through interpretation, so the comparison is weak and dishonors the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا التأويل ضعيف، وذلك كون آدم مثالا للكفار الجاحدين بالله ليس بشيء،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers either a fresh narrative or a link to the Prophet's command not to hasten revelation: Adam's forgotten charge warns him more strongly.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r9.anchor: وإما أن يجعل تعلقه أنه لما عهد إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يعجل بالقرآن، مثل له بنبي قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says عهد here means a testament or injunction.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes نسي as leaving the command, not absent-minded forgetting, since such forgetfulness cannot incur punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r11.anchor: «ونسي» معناه ترك ونسيان الذهول لا يمكن هنا لأنه لا يتعلق بالناسي عقاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya defines عزم as resolve to persist in a belief; Adam believed he should not eat but failed to hold to it when Satan tempted him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r12.anchor: والعزم المضي على المعتقد في أي شيء كان وآدم عليه السلام قد كان يعتقد ألا يأكل من الشجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r13.claim: The charge was not to eat from the tree, and Adam was warned that Iblīs was his enemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r13.anchor: والشيء الذي عهد إلى آدم هو ألا يأكل من الشجرة، وأعلم مع ذلك أن إبليس عدو له.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda explain the lack of resolve as lack of patience resisting the tree and steadiness in keeping the command.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r14.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة: لم نجد له صبرا عن أكل الشجرة، ومواظبة على التزام الأمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r15.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r15.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says عزم linguistically means patience and firmness in guarding oneself from sin; he links it to 46:35.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115/r15.anchor: قال النحاس: وكذلك هو في اللغة يقال: لفلان عزم أي صبر وثبات على التحفظ من المعاصي حتى يسلم منها، ومنه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعطية العوفي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī explain it as guarding the command; Adam failed to infer that a similar tree was included in the prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وعطية العوفي: حفظا لما أمر به أي لم يتحفظ مما نهيته حتى نسي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعطية العوفي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r2.claim: On their account, Satan promised the named tree would grant eternity; Adam refused it but did not infer the similar tree was also forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أن إبليس قال له: إن أكلتها خلدت في الجنة يعني عين تلك الشجرة، فلم يطعه فدعاه إلى نظير تلك الشجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وعطية العوفي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r3.claim: They say Adam forgot by losing knowledge through failure to reason; one who knows an act is sinful cannot forget it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وعطية العوفي: حفظا لما أمر به أي لم يتحفظ مما نهيته حتى نسي، وذهب عن علم ذلك بترك الاستدلال

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd explains عزم as preserving God's command.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: «عزما» محافظة على أمر الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains عزم as determination in the matter.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysān understands it as neither insistence nor intention to return to the sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r6.anchor: ابن كيسان: إصرارا ولا إضمارا للعود إلى الذنب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r7.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the first explanation, patience and steadiness in keeping the command, best fits the wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r7.anchor: قال القشيري: والأول أقرب إلى تأويل الكلام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r8.claim: Some infer that Adam was not among the messengers of resolve because God says He found no resolve in him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r8.anchor: ولهذا قال قوم: آدم لم يكن من أولي العزم من الرسل لأن الله تعالى قال: { ولم نجد له عزما }.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r9.speaker: المعظم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r9.claim: Most scholars hold that all messengers were messengers of resolve.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r9.anchor: وقال المعظم: كل الرسل أولو العزم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r10.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r10.claim: A report says every prophet erred or considered a sin except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā; excluding Adam would therefore exclude all but Yaḥyā.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r10.anchor: وفي الخبر: «ما من نبي إلا وقد أخطأ أو هم بخطيئة ما خلا يحيى بن زكريا»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r11.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r11.claim: Abū Umāma says that if humanity's understanding were weighed against Adam's, Adam's would outweigh it, despite the verse saying he lacked resolve.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:115#2/r11.anchor: وقد قال أبو أمامة: لو أن أحلام بني آدم جمعت منذ خلق الله الخلق إلى يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r1.claim: This is the sixth Qurʾānic telling of Adam’s story, following al-Baqara, al-Aʿrāf, al-Ḥijr, al-Isrāʾ, and al-Kahf.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r1.anchor: المرة السادسة من قصة آدم عليه السلام في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r2.claim: The story fulfills the earlier promise to relate reports of the past in 20:99.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r2.anchor: انجازا للوعد في قوله : { كذالك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق }

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r3.claim: Placed after the Qurʾān’s warnings, Adam’s disobedience shows that humans have long failed to guard against Satan’s whispers: even a direct warning that he was an enemy did not prevent Adam’s lapse.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r3.anchor: كأنه قال : إن طاعة بني آدم للشيطان وتركهم التحفظ من وساوسه

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r4.claim: After the command to seek more knowledge, Adam’s forgetfulness despite repeated warning illustrates human weakness and the need to ask God for knowledge and protection from forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r4.anchor: ذكر بعده قصة آدم عليه السلام فإنه بعدما عهد الله إليه وبالغ في تجديد العهد وتحذيره من العدو نسي

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.claim: The Prophet’s excessive zeal in religious effort is juxtaposed with Adam’s negligence: humans may err through either excess or shortfall.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r5.anchor: فلما وصفه بالإفراط وصف آدم بالتفريط في ذلك فإنه تساهل في ذلك ولم يتحفظ

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.claim: The Prophet may have worried that the prohibition implied wrongdoing; the story reassures him that his haste sprang from devotion and care for revelation, unlike Adam’s lapse through neglect.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r6.anchor: فقيل له : إن كنت فعلت ما نهيت عنه فإنما فعلته حرصا منك على العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r7.claim: God’s covenant here means a divine command or prohibition, as when a king gives instructions or a charge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r7.anchor: فلا شك أن المراد بالعهد أمر من الله تعالى أو نهي منه

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r8.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r8.claim: The exegetes say Adam was charged not to eat from the tree or even approach it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون : عهدنا إليه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة ولا يقربها

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r9.claim: One interpretation of min qablu is before those who received the Qurʾānic warnings.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r9.anchor: أحدها : من قبل هؤلاء الذين صرفنا لهم الوعيد في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes min qablu to mean before Adam ate from the tree, when God had charged him not to eat from it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r10.anchor: وثانيها : قال ابن عباس : من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes min qablu to mean before Muḥammad and the Qurʾān.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r11.anchor: أي من قبل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن وهو قول الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r12.claim: One view takes nasiya in its ordinary opposite-of-remembering sense: Adam was reproached for insufficient attention and retention, which led to forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r12.anchor: وإنما عوتب على ترك التحفظ والمبالغة في الضبط حتى تولد منه النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan swore that Adam never disobeyed except through forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r13.anchor: وكان الحسن رحمه الله يقول : والله ما عصى قط إلا بنسيان

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r14.claim: A second view reads nasiya as left or neglected: Adam abandoned the charge to avoid the tree and ate its fruit.

RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r15.claim: A variant, fa-nassāhu al-shayṭān, makes Satan the one who caused Adam to forget; on this reading, the act may have been deliberate without interpretation or committed under an interpretation, as discussed in al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v22p106#2/r15.anchor: وقرىء : فنسي أي فنساه الشيطان ، وعلى هذا التقدير

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r1.claim: Wajada may mean knew, as in this phrase, or its opposite of nonexistence, yielding the sense that Adam lacked resolve.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r1.anchor: الوجود يجوز أن يكون بمعنى العلم ومنه ولم نجد له عزما وأن يكون نقيض العدم

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r2.claim: ʿAzm means firm determination and steadfastness.

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r3.claim: One possible gloss is that Adam lacked resolve to persist in sin, which makes the phrase closer to praise.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r3.anchor: ولم نجد له عزما على القيام على المعصية فيكون إلى المدح أقرب

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r4.claim: Alternatively, he lacked resolve to abandon the sin.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد ولم نجد له عزما على ترك المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r5.claim: Another possibility is that Adam lacked resolve to guard himself against heedlessness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r5.anchor: أو لم نجد له عزما على التحفظ والاحتراز عن الغفلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r6.speaker: author
