RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r6.claim: If Adam’s mistake came through personal reasoning, the phrase may mean that he lacked resolve to exercise due care in how he reasoned.
RAZI-FULL:v22p107/r6.anchor: إذا قلنا : إنه عليه السلام إنما أخطأ بالاجتهاد

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r12.claim: Adam lacked the strength and resolve to maintain obedience, and so came to bear the mark of disobedience.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r12.anchor: لم تجد له قوة بالكمال ، وانكماشا في مراعاة الأمر حتى وقعت عليه سمة العصيان

QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r13.claim: The verse means Adam had no resolve to persist in opposition; any contrary action arose through forgetfulness, even as he followed some demands of the command.
QUSHAYRI:v2p276/r13.anchor: ويقال : { لم نجد له عزما } : على الإصرار على المخالفة

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r1.claim: The account of Adam's lapse reassures his descendants so they will not despair of God's mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r1.anchor: شرح قصة آدم - عليه السلام - لأولاده على حجة التسكين لقلوبهم حتى لا يقنطوا من رحمة الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r2.claim: Here nasiya means actual forgetfulness, and forgetfulness had not been lifted from people at that time.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فنسى } من النسيان ، ولم يكن في وقته النسيان مرفوعا عن الناس

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r3.claim: God reproached Adam by saying he forgot, then stated the mitigating fact that he lacked resolve.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r3.anchor: ويقال عاتبه بقوله : { فنسى } ثم أظهر عذره فقال : { ولم نجد له عزما }

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r1.claim: God's pact with Adam was the prohibition against approaching the tree.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r1.anchor: The pact that God made with Adam refers to His telling him not to approach the tree

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r2.claim: “Aforetime” can mean before Adam ate from the tree or, more broadly, before Muhammad's prophethood and Quranic revelation.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r2.anchor: By aforetime is meant either before Adam’s actual eating from the tree or, more generally, before the coming of the Prophet Muhammad and the revelation of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r3.claim: “He forgot” can mean Adam forgot his pact or abandoned it.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r3.anchor: He forgot denotes Adam’s forgetting his pact (Q) or abandoning it

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that Adam forgot and so his descendants forgot.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said, “Adam forgot, and thus his progeny forgot.”

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r5.claim: Adam is a model for humanity; God taught him all the names.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r5.anchor: Adam is the model for human beings to follow, since God taught Adam the names, all of them

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r6.speaker: Shams-i Tabrīzī
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r6.claim: Shams says Adam forgot only once, so people should remember that one lapse is enough; his father's custom was to forget once.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r6.anchor: Shams-i Tabrīzī (disappeared in 644/1247), people should keep in mind that Adam only forgot one time

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r7.claim: One interpretation is that Adam lacked resolve to disobey God, so his error was unintentional because Satan deceived him.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r7.anchor: We found no resoluteness in him can mean that God did not find in Adam the resolve to disobey Him

STUDYQURAN:20:115/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that Adam lacked resolve to obey the prohibition; some connect this to his not being among the resolute messengers.
STUDYQURAN:20:115/r8.anchor: Or We found no resoluteness in him can mean that God did not find in Adam the moral resolve to obey His Prohibition

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r1.claim: Those who disregard the warnings in this Qur'an repeat an ancient pattern: their father Adam violated God's covenant and obeyed his enemy.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي} [طه: 115] يقول: فترك

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r2.claim: God warned Adam that Satan was an enemy to him and his wife and must not drive them from the Garden; Satan whispered, Adam obeyed and incurred punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r2.anchor: ولقد وصينا آدم وقلنا له: {إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة} [طه: 117] فوسوس إليه الشيطان فأطاعه

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r3.claim: Min qablu refers to Adam's breach before the warned people discussed in the passage disregard God's warning.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r3.anchor: وعنى جل ثناؤه بقوله: {من قبل} [البقرة: 25] هؤلاء الذين أخبر أنه صرف لهم الوعيد في هذا القرآن

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r4.claim: Nasiya means Adam abandoned God's covenant.

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses nasiya as he abandoned it.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي} [طه: 115] يقول: فترك

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r6.claim: Mujāhid says Adam abandoned his Lord's command.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {فنسي} [طه: 115] قال: ترك أمر ربه

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd connects the covenant with 20:117-120, saying Adam forgot it and lacked resolve; he would not have obeyed the envious enemy if resolved, and disobeyed God who honored him and commanded angels to bow.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] قال: قال له {يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك

TAB-FULL:v16p182/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-insān was named so because a covenant was made with him and he forgot.
TAB-FULL:v16p182/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: إنما سمي الإنسان لأنه عهد إليه فنسي

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r1.claim: Qatada glosses Adam's lack of ʿazm as lack of patience.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] أي صبرا

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r2.speaker: عطية
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r2.claim: Atiyya interprets the phrase as Adam's failure to preserve what God commanded him.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r2.anchor: عن عطية، {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] قال: حفظا لما أمرته

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise explains ʿazm as keeping or preserving the entrusted command.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] يقول: لم نجد له حفظا

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd defines ʿazm as guarding what God commanded Adam to preserve and holding fast to it.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] قال: العزم: المحافظة على ما أمره الله تبارك وتعالى بحفظه، والتمسك به

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r5.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas takes the wording to mean that God did not create or grant Adam resolve.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115] يقول: لم نجعل له عزما

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r6.claim: Abu Umama says Adam's intelligence would outweigh that of all humans combined, although the verse says he lacked resolve.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r6.anchor: عن أبي أمامة، قال: لو أن أحلام بني آدم، جمعت منذ يوم خلق الله تعالى آدم إلى يوم الساعة

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r7.claim: Al-Tabari says the root sense of ʿazm is the heart's firm determination and intention; preserving something and patience also arise from that firmness.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r7.anchor: وأصل العزم اعتقاد القلب على الشيء، يقال منه: عزم فلان على كذا: إذا اعتقد عليه ونواه

TAB-FULL:v16p183/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r8.claim: Al-Tabari's preferred sense is that Adam lacked firmness of heart to fulfill God's covenant and preserve what was entrusted to him.
TAB-FULL:v16p183/r8.anchor: لا معنى لذلك أبلغ مما بينه الله تبارك وتعالى، وهو قوله: {ولم نجد له عزما} [طه: 115]

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says Adam was charged to obey no one besides God; he forgot the covenant by looking to the garden with his eye rather than attending to God with his inner secret.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم ﴾ قال : عهدنا إلى آدم

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r2.claim: Ja'far says Adam was charged not to forget God in any state, but the garden's delight distracted him from its giver; expulsion taught him that true bliss is nearness to God, not food and drink.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : عهدنا إلى آدم أن لا ينسانا في حال ونسينا

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says Adam lacked resolve because, on entering the garden, he attended to his own deed rather than God's grace.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ﴿ لم نجد له عزما ﴾ لم يطالع في دخول

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r4.claim: Al-Wasiti explains the lack of resolve as inability to restrain himself; God concealed Adam from witnessing himself so he could see signs of servitude as admonition and adornment.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ﴿ فنسي ولم نجد له عزما ﴾ أي قوة

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r5.claim: Al-Wasiti says 'he forgot' has two senses, distinguishing one who forgets in God's presence from one who forgets in absence.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ' فنسي ' له وجهان

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r6.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti supports the distinction with the Prophet's report that error and forgetfulness are lifted from his community.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان '

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r7.claim: Another says Adam forgot God's command at the moment he partook of the fruit.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : نسي في وقت التناول مطالعة الأمر

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r8.speaker: أبو القاسم النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r8.claim: Al-Nasrabadi distinguishes a sin that obliges one to seek forgiveness from a sin one is made to commit and is excused for.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r8.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم النصرآباذي يقول : ذنب لزمته فوجب عليك

SULAMI:v1p449#6/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r9.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r9.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl interprets Adam's lack of resolve as returning to the sin a second time.
SULAMI:v1p449#6/r9.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل في قوله : ﴿ ولم نجد له عزما ﴾

TABATABAI:20:115/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r1.claim: The compact Adam story recounts the couple’s expulsion after Satan’s whisper and chiefly explains the institution of religion and the reward for guidance or punishment for turning away.
TABATABAI:20:115/r1.anchor: بيان قصة دخول آدم وزوجة الجنة وخروجهما منها بوسوسة من الشيطان وقضائه تعالى عند ذلك بتشريع الدين وسعادة من اتبع الهدى

TABATABAI:20:115/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r2.claim: Its mention of Adam’s repentance also connects the account to the earlier promise of forgiveness to those who repent, believe, and act righteously.
TABATABAI:20:115/r2.anchor: ذكرها توبة آدم بقوله فيما تقدم { وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى }

TABATABAI:20:115/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r3.claim: The story depicts human earthly nature: God created people excellently, surrounded them with blessings, and placed them in a balanced garden, warning against excess and attachment to worldly desire.
TABATABAI:20:115/r3.anchor: فقد خلقه الله سبحانه في أحسن تقويم وغمره في نعمه التي لا تحصى وأسكنه جنة الاعتدال ومنعه عن تعديه بالخروج إلى جانب الإسراف

TABATABAI:20:115/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r4.claim: Satan tempts people to forget God and imagine that attachment to the world grants mastery over causes and lasting pleasure; worldly means fail, suffering compounds, and the person loses the garden of blessing.
TABATABAI:20:115/r4.anchor: الذي يزين له الدنيا ويصور له ويخيل إليه أنه لو تعلق بها ونسي ربه اكتسب بذلك سلطانا على الأسباب الكونية

TABATABAI:20:115/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r5.claim: Adam’s episode preceded the legislation of religion; his garden was a barzakhic, non-worldly life, and the tree prohibition was advisory, so its violation brought an inevitable consequence rather than a legal punishment.
TABATABAI:20:115/r5.anchor: إلا أن واقعته عليه السلام كانت قبل تشريع أصل الدين وجنته جنة برزخية ممثلة في عيشة غير دنيوية فكان النهي لذلك إرشاديا لا مولويا

TABATABAI:20:115/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r6.claim: A covenant here is a charge or admonition; the word is also used for edicts and codes.
TABATABAI:20:115/r6.anchor: المراد بالعهد الوصية وبهذا المعنى يطلق على الفرامين والدساتير العهود

TABATABAI:20:115/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r7.claim: Nisyan means forgetting and may also stand for abandoning something, since forgetting entails leaving it.
TABATABAI:20:115/r7.anchor: والنسيان معروف وربما يكنى به عن الترك لأنه لازمه إذ الشيء إذا نسي ترك

TABATABAI:20:115/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115/r8.claim: ʿAzm means a firm intention or resolve toward something.

TABATABAI:20:116-117/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r2.claim: The verse means God charged Adam earlier, but he abandoned the charge and lacked firm resolve or patience to preserve it; the charge was the ban on eating from the tree.
TABATABAI:20:116-117/r2.anchor: فالمعنى وأقسم لقد وصينا آدم من قبل فترك الوصية ولم نجد له قصدا جازما إلى حفظها أو صبرا عليها

TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.claim: The close echoes Adam's forgetfulness: his garden story prefigures his descendants, the tree prohibition represents later divine guidance, and their sins are forgetting God's reminders; unlike them, Adam faced an advisory ban before religious law.
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.anchor: وانعطف بذلك آخر الكلام إلى أوله وهو معصية آدم التي سماها نسيانا لعهده

TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r1.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r1.claim: Al-Qummī's commentary says Adam's forgetting concerned the prohibition against eating from the tree.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r1.anchor: تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما } قال فيما نهاه عنه من أكل الشجرة

TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r2.speaker: أحدهما عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r2.claim: In a report transmitted by al-ʿAyyāshī from Jamīl ibn Darraj, one of the two Imams answers that Adam did not forget: Iblis had just reminded him of the prohibition; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats the literal-forgetting claim as contrary to the Qurʾān.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r2.anchor: عن جميل بن دراج عن بعض أصحابنا عن أحدهما عليه السلام قال سألته كيف أخذ الله آدم بالنسيان

TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r3.claim: A report in al-Kāfī, from Abū Jaʿfar through Abū Ḥamza, says God covenanted with Adam, who forgot and ate when the appointed time arrived; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this report is weak.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r3.anchor: بإسناده عن أبي حمزة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله تبارك وتعالى عهد إلى آدم

TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r4.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās takes “no firm resolve” to mean Adam had no intent to disobey; he used it to argue that ʿAlī's possible marriage proposal was not a resolved offense against the Prophet, but a passing thought.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r4.anchor: وهذا القول منسوب إلى ابن عباس والأصل فيه ما رواه في الدر المنثور عن الزبير بن بكار

TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r6.claim: The report continues with ʿUmar worrying that ʿAlī might become proud if he governed; Ibn ʿAbbās replies that ʿAlī had not resolved to anger the Prophet and that passing thoughts can occur even to learned jurists.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#3/r6.anchor: قلت يا أمير المؤمنين إن صاحبنا من قد علمت والله ما نقول إنه غير ولا عدل ولا أسخط رسول الله

TABATABAI:20:115-126#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#4/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās: it assumes literal forgetfulness and takes resolve as intent to sin, contradicts 7:20, and does not fit the surrounding account; he doubts Ibn ʿAbbās held it.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#4/r1.anchor: على أن الآية بالمعنى الذي ذكره لا تناسب سياق الآيات السابقة عليها ولا اللاحقة

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī invokes unequivocal reports of ʿAlī's purity from sin, including the reports of the Two Weighty Things, the Station, and ʿAlī with the truth and the truth with ʿAlī.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r1.anchor: الروايات القطعية الدالة على نزاهة ساحة علي عليه السلام من المعصية كخبر الثقلين وخبر المنزلة

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r2.claim: A report in al-Kāfī and al-ʿIlal, from Abū Jaʿfar through Jābir ibn Yazīd, says Adam's covenant concerned Muhammad and the Imams among his descendants; Adam left it without firm resolve, while the resolute prophets affirmed it.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن يزيد عن أبى جعفر عليه السلام في قول الله تعالى

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r3.claim: The fuller al-Kāfī report describes the primordial testimony and covenants to divinity, prophethood, and wilāya: the resolute prophets affirm them, while Adam hesitates without denying them and the verse is applied to him.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r3.anchor: أخذ الميثاق من آدم عليه السلام ومن أولي العزم من الرسل بالربوبية والنبوة والولاية

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies the covenant-to-the-Imams report as an inner meaning, returning covenants to the reality of divine wilāya, not as the lexical interpretation of the verse.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r4.anchor: والمعنى المذكور في الرواية من بطن القرآن أرجع فيه الأحكام إلى حقيقتها والعهود إلى تأويلها

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r5.claim: The twelve verses narrate one story; reading the opening as a reference to wilāya would leave the tree prohibition, a central element, unstated, and 20:117 cannot replace it. The relevant al-Aʿrāf and al-Baqara passages were revealed later than Ṭā Hā.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r5.anchor: ولو حملت الآية الأولى على هذا المعنى تفسيرا لم يبق في الآيات ما يدل على النهي عن أكل الشجرة

TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r6.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r6.claim: A report in al-Manāqib attributed to al-Bāqir inserts words naming Muhammad, ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and the Imams into the verse; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī identifies such wording as a report of textual distortion.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#5/r6.anchor: كما في المناقب عن الباقر عليه السلام ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل كلمات في محمد وعلي وفاطمة

TABRISI:20:114-115/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:114-115/r11.claim: God charged Adam not to approach or eat from the tree; Adam left that command undone.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r11.anchor: معناه أمرناه وأوصينا إليه أن لا يقرب الشجرة ولا يأكل منها فترك الأمر عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:114-115/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:114-115/r12.claim: The phrase can mean that Adam lacked a firm, settled resolve.

TABRISI:20:114-115/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r13.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
TABRISI:20:114-115/r13.claim: Adam forgot through inadvertence and did not resolve to sin; he erred without deliberate intent.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه فنسي من النسيان الذي هو السهو ولم نجد له عزما على الذنب لأنه أخطأ ولم يتعمد عن ابن زيد وجماعة

TABRISI:20:114-115/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r14.speaker: عطية
TABRISI:20:114-115/r14.claim: Atiyya takes the phrase to mean that Adam did not retain what he had been commanded.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r14.anchor: وقيل: ولم نجد له حفظا لما أمر به عن عطية

TABRISI:20:114-115/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r15.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:20:114-115/r15.claim: Qatada interprets Adam’s lack of resolve as a lack of patience.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r15.anchor: ولم نجد له حفظا لما أمر به عن عطية. وقيل: صبرا عن قتادة

TABRISI:20:114-115/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:114-115/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says humanity’s plight stems from Adam being charged with a command and then forgetting it.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r16.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال إنما أخذ الإنسان من أنه عهد إليه فنسي

TABRISI:20:114-115/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:114-115/r17.claim: One view is that Adam forgot the warning that eating from the tree would expel him from Paradise.

TABRISI:20:114-115/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:114-115/r18.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:114-115/r18.claim: Another view is that Adam forgot God’s warning that the devil was an enemy to him and his wife.
TABRISI:20:114-115/r18.anchor: والثاني: أنه نسي قول الله سبحانه

TABRISI:20:115/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:115/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:115/r1.claim: A further view is that Adam forgot the prohibition applied to the whole kind of tree and thought it referred only to the particular tree.
TABRISI:20:115/r1.anchor: والثالث أنه نسي الاستدلال على أن النهي عن الجنس

TABRISI:20:115/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:115/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:115/r2.claim: The Adam episode follows the account of the Qur’an’s varied signs by urging remembrance, so people will not forget their covenant as Adam did.
TABRISI:20:115/r2.anchor: لما ذكر تصريف الآيات والقرآن وإن بها يتذكر أمره سبحانه بالتذكر

TABRISI:20:115/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:115/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:115/r3.claim: The verses connect the command not to hurry with trust in God to preserve the Qur’an, since Adam forgot what had been entrusted to him.
TABRISI:20:115/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنه إتصل بقوله { ولا تعجل بالقرآن } أي لا تعجل خوف النسيان للفظه

TABRISI:20:115/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:115/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:115/r4.claim: Abu Muslim connects the Adam passage to the account of earlier events, as another story from the reports of the past.
TABRISI:20:115/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه عطف على قوله { وكذلك نقص عليك } من أنباء ما قد سبق

THALABI:v6p262#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p262#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p262#2/r1.claim: The warning is that if these people neglect God's Qurʾānic admonitions and commands, their father Adam did so before them by abandoning the instruction entrusted to him.
THALABI:v6p262#2/r1.anchor: وإن يضيع هؤلاء الذين نصرف لهم في القرآن الوعيد عهدي ويخالفوا أمري ويتركوا طاعتي

THALABI:v6p262#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p262#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p262#2/r2.claim: Most commentators take Adam's forgetting as leaving or abandoning the command, as in the verse that says God “forgot” those who forgot Him, meaning He left them in Hell.
THALABI:v6p262#2/r2.anchor: فنسي فترك الأمر والعهد، نظيره قوله نسوا الله فنسيهم أي تركوا أمر الله فتركهم الله في النار

THALABI:v6p263/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p263/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says Adam forgot God's charge; had he been resolute, he would not have obeyed the envious Iblīs over the God who honored him, and Adam may be held responsible for this forgetting although it is lifted from us today.
THALABI:v6p263/r1.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نسي ما عهد الله إليه في ذلك، ولو كان له عزم ما أطاع عدوه إبليس

THALABI:v6p263/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p263/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ʿazm as retaining or remembering what Adam was commanded.
THALABI:v6p263/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حفظا لما أمر به، قتادة ومقاتل: صبرا

THALABI:v6p263/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r3.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
THALABI:v6p263/r3.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil interpret ʿazm as patience.
THALABI:v6p263/r3.anchor: قتادة ومقاتل: صبرا، ابن زيد: محافظة على أمر الله

THALABI:v6p263/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p263/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes ʿazm as maintaining God's command and holding fast to it.
THALABI:v6p263/r4.anchor: ابن زيد: محافظة على أمر الله وتمسكا به، الضحاك: صريمة أمر

THALABI:v6p263/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r5.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p263/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses ʿazm as a firm resolve.
THALABI:v6p263/r5.anchor: الضحاك: صريمة أمر، عطية: رأيا، وقيل: جزما

THALABI:v6p263/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r6.speaker: عطية
THALABI:v6p263/r6.claim: ʿAṭiyya interprets ʿazm as an opinion or considered judgment.
THALABI:v6p263/r6.anchor: عطية: رأيا، وقيل: جزما، ابن كيسان: إصرارا وإضمارا

THALABI:v6p263/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r7.claim: Another gloss is determination; Ibn Kaysān explains it as commitment and an inward resolve not to return to sin.
THALABI:v6p263/r7.anchor: ابن كيسان: إصرارا وإضمارا على العود إلى الذنب ثانيا

THALABI:v6p263/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r8.claim: The basic sense of ʿazm is intention and the heart's resolve toward something.
THALABI:v6p263/r8.anchor: وأصل العزم النية واعتقاد القلب على الشيء

THALABI:v6p263/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
THALABI:v6p263/r9.claim: Abū Umāma says that if all human forbearance since Adam's creation were weighed against Adam's alone, Adam's would outweigh it, despite the verse saying he lacked resolve.
THALABI:v6p263/r9.anchor: قال أبو أمامة: لو أن أحلام بني آدم جمعت منذ يوم خلق الله سبحانه آدم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r1.claim: Adam's forgetting means that he abandoned the covenant.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r2.claim: ʿAzm means a firmly resolved judgment or purpose.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#2/r2.anchor: ولم نجد له عزما} أي رأيا معزوما عليه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r1.claim: God's covenant with Adam means that He commanded and enjoined him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r1.anchor: {ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم} أي: أمرناه وأوصينا إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي، السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Suddī say Adam was charged not to eat from the tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي والسدي: (عهدنا إليه ألا يأكل من الشجرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam was told not to approach the tree.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī takes “before” to mean before Adam ate from the tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: (من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r5.claim: Another reading takes “before” as before the people who broke God's covenant and abandoned faith; these are the people mentioned in 20:113, and Adam too had been covenanted with.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: (من قبل هؤلاء الذين فقضوا عهدي وتركوا الإيمان بي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses Adam's forgetting as abandoning God's covenant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says Adam left undone what he had been commanded.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the forgetting as abandoning God's covenant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r9.claim: The author says all the reported views agree that nasiya here means “left” or “abandoned.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r9.anchor: هذا قول الجميع في أن نسي هاهنا: ترك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r10.claim: Abū Isḥāq says “he forgot” means “he left,” since one is not held accountable for forgetting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ({فنسي} هاهنا فترك؛ لأن الناسي لا يؤاخذ بنسيانه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd reads this as literal forgetting, but the author rejects that: forgetfulness is not accountable, and Satan reminded Adam and Eve of the prohibition in 7:20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p542#2/r11.anchor: وحمل ابن زيد النسيان هاهنا على الذي هو ضد الذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r1.claim: ʿAzm is a firm resolve of the heart to do something and the self's firm commitment to act.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r1.anchor: معنى العزم: عقد القلب على أمر يفعله، وهو توطين النفس على الفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Ibn ʿAbbās takes the phrase to mean that Adam lacked patience to refrain from eating the tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد صبرا عن أكل الشجرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r3.claim: Adam did not persevere in the resolve he had made to avoid what he was forbidden to eat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أنه لم يصبر على ما وطن عليه نفسه من ترك ما نهي عن أكله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan likewise glosses the phrase as lacking patience concerning what Adam was forbidden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r4.anchor: وهو معنى قول الحسن: (صبرا عما نهي عنه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r5.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī explains it as not holding to what God had entrusted him with regarding the command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r5.anchor: وقال عطية العوفي: (عن ما حفظنا لما أمر به)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r6.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r6.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the lack of resolve as lack of patience in the face of sins.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim takes ʿazm as a firmly held judgment or decision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسلم: (رأيا معزوما عليه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r8.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r8.claim: An unattributed view takes it as a firm commitment, which Adam failed to keep when he obeyed his envious enemy Iblīs, who refused to prostrate to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p543/r8.anchor: وقيل: (عقدا ثابتا حيث أطاع عدوه إبليس الذي حسده وأبى أن يسجد له)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r4.claim: God commanded and instructed Adam before these people who disobeyed and broke the covenant by denying Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r4.anchor: { ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم } أمرنا وأوصينا إليه { من قبل } هؤلاء الذين تركوا أمري، ونقضوا عهدي في تكذيبك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r5.claim: Adam forgot by abandoning his command; lacking resolve means failing to retain it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:114-115/r5.anchor: { فنسي } فترك ما أمر به { ولم نجد له عزما } حفظا لما أمر به.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r1.claim: Adam broke the covenant by leaving God’s command not to eat from the tree.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r1.anchor:
يعني: فترد العهد.
يقول: فترك ما أمر به: ألا يأكل من الشجرة.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r1.claim: نسيان may mean loss of memory, its basic opposite of retaining or remembering, as in the forgotten fish and Moses' request not to be blamed for forgetting.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r1.anchor: ضد الحفظ، كقوله: فإني نسيت الحوت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271#2/r2.claim: نسيان can also mean abandonment: Adam abandoned the command; people abandoned belief in Judgment, God abandoned them, and believers should not forsake kindness.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r1.claim: Exegetes connect this Adam account with the warning in 20:113 that admonitions recur: humanity’s faulty response to divine warnings dates back to its first ancestor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r1.anchor: Genellikle müfessirler bu âyetlerle Kur’an’da uyarılara tekrar tekrar yer verildiğini bildiren 113. âyet arasında bağ kurarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.claim: Earlier passages in Ṣād and al-Aʿrāf recount Adam, Iblis’s disobedience, the couple’s conditional stay in the garden, Satan’s enticement and their expulsion; retelling these matters in different contexts and styles is characteristic of the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r2.anchor: Yine A‘râf sûresinde Âdem’e –yasak ağaca yaklaşmamaları koşuluyla– eşiyle birlikte cennette kalma imkânı verildiğinden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r3.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r3.claim: Unlike earlier accounts, this passage says Adam’s repentance was accepted and that he was chosen, meaning commissioned as a prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r3.anchor: Burada önceki değinilerden farklı olarak Âdem’in tövbesinin kabul edildiğinden hatta onun seçkin kılındığından yani peygamber olarak görevlendirildiğinden (Şevkânî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r4.claim: The account rejects inherited original sin: despite Adam’s error, people are not born sinful as Christian belief holds, since Adam repented and was forgiven.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r4.anchor: insanlar –hıristiyan inancında kabul edildiğinin aksine– dünyaya ilk atalarının işlediği günah sebebiyle günahkar olarak gelmezler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r5.claim: Each person is tested in an environment prone to sin and with capacities usable for good or evil, and can seek forgiveness directly from God without an intermediary.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r5.anchor: her insan bir taraftan günah işlemeye yatkın bir ortamda ve iyiliğe de kötülüğe de kullanılabilecek yeteneklerle donatılmış olarak sınava tâbi olacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r6.claim: This principle undercuts the Christian doctrine that God sacrificed Jesus to cleanse humanity of original sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r6.anchor: Hıristiyanlığın temel akîde esaslarından olan rabbin insanlığı bu aslî günahtan arındırmak için Îsâ’yı kurban ettiği iddiası temelden yoksun kalmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r7.claim: The placement after Sūrat Maryam, which explains Jesus’s birth and condemns mistaken assumptions about it, creates a thematic connection with this account of Adam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r7.anchor: bu sûrenin Hz. Îsâ’nın nasıl dünyaya geldiğini açıklayan ve bu konudaki yanlış kabulleri mahkûm eden Meryem sûresinden sonra inmiş olması arasında bir anlam örgüsü bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r8.claim: The authors render the phrase as “We had taken a covenant from Adam.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r8.anchor: 115. âyetin “Âdem’den söz almıştık” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz kısmını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r9.speaker: bazıları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r9.claim: Some understand the phrase as “We had conveyed Our command to Adam,” specifically the warning not to obey Satan, his and his wife’s enemy, explained in 20:117.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r9.anchor: “Âdem’e buyruğumuzu bildirmiştik” şeklinde anlayanlar da vardır. Bu yorumda söz konusu olan buyruk, kendisinin ve eşinin düşmanı olan şeytana uymamasıyla ilgili uyarı olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r10.speaker: bir yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r10.claim: One interpretation is that Adam first resolved not to eat from the forbidden tree but failed to remain firm under Satan’s temptation or attractive offer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r10.anchor: Bir yoruma göre, burada Âdem’in önce yasak ağaçtan yememeye karar vermişken, şeytanın kışkırtması karşısında kararlı davranamadığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r11.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that Adam did not persist in committing the sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r11.anchor: Diğer bir yoruma göre ise burada maksat, Âdem’in günah işlemede ısrarlı davranmamış olduğudur (Şevkânî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r12.speaker: Taberî ve Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r12.claim: Though the verb literally means “he forgot,” exegetes more often explain it as Adam’s abandoning his Lord’s command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r12.anchor: lafzan “unuttu” anlamına gelen fiil daha çok “Rabbinin buyruğunu terketti” şeklinde açıklanmıştır (Taberî

BURHAN:v1p35/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p35/r1.claim: Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr devoted a work to Qur'anic coherence, and Fakhr al-Din al-Razi's commentary contains much on the subject.
BURHAN:v1p35/r1.anchor: وقد أفرده بالتصنيف الأستاذ أبو جعفر بن الزبير شيخ الشيخ أبى حيان وتفسير الإمام فخر الدين فيه شىء كثير من ذلك

BURHAN:v1p35/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p35/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p35/r2.claim: Munasaba means nearness or likeness; in Qur'anic arrangement it is any general or specific relation between openings and endings, including rational, sensory, imaginative, causal, contrasting, or externally ordered links.
BURHAN:v1p35/r2.anchor: واعلم أن المناسبة علم شريف تحزر به العقول ويعرف به قدر القائل فيما يقول والمناسبة فى اللغة المقاربة

BURHAN:v1p35/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p35/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p35/r3.claim: Coherence binds parts of speech together, strengthens their relation, and makes the composition resemble a firmly joined building.
BURHAN:v1p35/r3.anchor: وفائدته جعل أجزاء الكلام بعضها آخذا بأعناق بعض فيقوى بذلك الارتباط ويصير التأليف حاله حال البناء المحكم

BURHAN:v1p35/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p35/r4.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BURHAN:v1p35/r4.claim: Commentators often neglect this subtle field, but al-Razi discusses it extensively and says most Qur'anic subtleties lie in ordering and connections.
BURHAN:v1p35/r4.anchor: وقد قل اعتناء المفسرين بهذا النوع لدقته وممن أكثر منه الإمام فخر الدين الرازى وقال فى تفسيره أكثر لطائف القرآن مودعة فى الترتيبات والروابط

BURHAN:v1p35/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p35/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
BURHAN:v1p35/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi calls the coherence of Qur'anic verses as one connected word a great science; after writing on al-Baqara, he says he found no bearers for the work and entrusted it to God.
BURHAN:v1p35/r5.anchor: قال القاضى أبو بكر بن العربى فى سراج المريدين ارتباط آى القرآن بعضها ببعض حتى تكون كالكلمة الواحدة

ITQAN:v3p288/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p288/r1.claim: The author lists major works on Qur'anic coherence by Ibn al-Zubayr and al-Biqāʿī, and his own Asrār al-Tanzīl and Tansuq al-Durar, which gathers sura relationships.
ITQAN:v3p288/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتأليف العلامة أبو جعفر بن الزبير شيخ أبي حيان في كتاب سماه

ITQAN:v3p288/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r2.speaker: فخر الدين
ITQAN:v3p288/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Dīn says that most of the Qur'an's subtle insights lie in its arrangements and connections.
ITQAN:v3p288/r2.anchor: وممن أكثر فيه الإمام فخر الدين وقال في تفسيره أكثر لطائف القرآن مودعة في الترتيبات والروابط

ITQAN:v3p288/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v3p288/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls the linking of verses into one coherent utterance a great science; after finding no one to carry it forward, he set his work aside for God.
ITQAN:v3p288/r3.anchor: وقال ابن العربي في ( سراج المريدين ) ارتباط آي القرآن بعضها ببعض حتى تكون كالكلمة الواحدة

ITQAN:v3p288/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r4.speaker: أبو بكر النيسابوري
ITQAN:v3p288/r4.claim: Abū Bakr al-Nīsābūrī first made the science of coherence prominent, asking why a verse or sura was placed beside another and criticizing Baghdad scholars for neglecting it.
ITQAN:v3p288/r4.anchor: وكان يقول على الكرسي إذا قرئ عليه لم جعلت هذه الآية إلى جنب هذه وما الحكمة في جعل هذه السورة

ITQAN:v3p288/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r5.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
ITQAN:v3p288/r5.claim: ʿIzz al-Dīn b. ʿAbd al-Salām accepts coherence when the subject is unified, but calls links contrived across distinct occasions and rulings in a revelation spanning over twenty years.
ITQAN:v3p288/r5.anchor: وقال الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام المناسبة علم حسن لكن يشترط في حسن ارتباط الكلام أن يقع في أمر متحد

ITQAN:v3p288/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p288/r6.speaker: ولي الدين الملوي
ITQAN:v3p288/r6.claim: Al-Malawī rejects the claim that no coherence should be sought merely because verses were revealed in separate circumstances.
ITQAN:v3p288/r6.anchor: وقال الشيخ ولي الدين الملوي قد وهم من قال لا يطلب للآي الكريمة مناسبة لأنها على حسب الوقائع المفرقة

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r14.claim: ʿAzm can mean patience or steadfast resolve, as in the command to be patient like the resolute messengers.
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r14.anchor: ولم نجد له عزما يعني صبرا كقوله تعالى في سورة الاحقاف فاصبر كما صبر

DAMGHANI:v1p335/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r12.claim: ʿAhd can mean a command: God had commanded Adam beforehand.
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r12.anchor: الثالث العهد الامر قوبه تعالى في سورة طه ولقد عهدنا الى ادم من قبل يعني امرنا ادم

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r10.claim: Nisyān can mean leaving or abandoning something, including leaving a verse un-abrogated.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r10.anchor: فوجه منهما النسيان الترك قوله تعالى في سورة طه ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي أي ترك
